official_measurement_examples.name: Planning Data snapshot limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data's Green Belt collection has 190 records from one provider and is a snapshot from annual local-authority returns; it explicitly may not reflect boundary changes since returns were submitted.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2024-25 national extent
official_measurement_examples.fact: Official statistics estimated 1,633,220 hectares of Green Belt at 31 March 2025, about 12.5% of England, with a net decrease of 660 hectares from the prior year.

official_measurement_examples.name: Grey belt definition
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current NPPF defines grey belt within Green Belt using previously developed land and/or weak contribution to specified Green Belt purposes, while excluding certain strongly protected footnote-7 areas.

official_measurement_examples.name: Grey belt is not automatic approval
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning guidance states identifying grey belt does not automatically mean allocation, release from Green Belt or approval; the wider NPPF tests still apply.

official_measurement_examples.name: Boundary alteration
official_measurement_examples.fact: Green Belt boundaries should only be altered where exceptional circumstances are fully evidenced and justified through plan preparation or updating.

official_measurement_examples.name: Release priority
official_measurement_examples.fact: Where release is necessary, current NPPF prioritises previously developed land, then grey belt that is not previously developed, then other Green Belt locations, subject to sustainable-development considerations.

official_measurement_examples.name: Safeguarded land distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Safeguarded land between an urban area and Green Belt is not allocated for development at the present time; permanent development normally follows a plan update proposing it.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 reform transition
official_measurement_examples.fact: The December 2025 NPPF reform document remains consultation material while the current Framework and confirmed guidance govern decisions; draft proposals must not be treated as enacted parcel rules.

core_rules: Green Belt national snapshot is not a live parcel boundary service
grey belt identification is not planning permission
grey belt identification does not automatically release land from Green Belt
Green Belt boundary changes require the relevant plan-making process
current NPPF must remain distinct from consultation drafts
Green Belt statistical area is not parcel development capacity
Green Belt core grouping is not a site allocation
safeguarded land is not currently allocated land
Golden Rules obligations are not a grant of planning permission
previously developed Green Belt land still requires proposal-specific policy assessment
Green Belt openness and purposes require site-specific assessment
footnote-7 constraints remain separate from Green Belt/grey belt classification
local-plan evidence must retain current/emerging/historic status
Green Belt geometry does not prove ownership or access rights
no parcel Green Belt clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
